en: After rising, he caught his breath,
Though sent onward, his eyes did not open,
He did not draw away from the truth,
His ancestral encampment was not subdued,
Taking the due of his companion,
Zhelzhetpes and the two heroes,
Gathering from their drenched souls,
Saddling the racehorse by the water,
Dressing in urgent haste,
He had a horse ridden into holy war,
The remaining soul of the gray beauty.
The elders came from the far bank.
The few who arrived sat down.
The gold fell into the embers.
The many who arrived were separated.
The fire fell into his breast.
Now strike, mighty falcon, amid the tumult.
Upon the hard road of doomsday,
He remained in the Creator’s hand alone,
Within God’s iron net,
Solely in the hand of death.
Turning wherever he could,
Vast-hearted hero Kenen,
Separated together from his people,
Endured much of this world.
His intent was dark and his heart poisonous.
He was trampled by the true enemy.
The gray-maned heroes entered the holy war.
Brave Kuman, companion of the soul,
Spoke his challenge and judged it firmly.
The orphan was beyond the wind’s reach.
No farming soul could pass your horse.
His eye gazed from afar.
Many rode out beyond the wind’s reach.
From delight beyond the eye’s reach,
He took a spear from the gray-maned heroes.
He was bound with no sheath remaining.
Behind you stood a lofty soul.
The worth of the slippery ones arrived.
He became khan over three peoples.
When he spoke world upon world of words,
A coin spun, beyond the wind’s reach.
The pattern stood upright.
What cast many stones outran the wind.
His soul belonged to the distant land.
Each man was worth a thousand,
Standing brow to brow,
Standing face to face,
They said Jeljetpes fixed his gaze on them,
The heroes who came between them,
Saying the Chinese had taken him,
They brought him down into their midst,
Saying the Chinese had taken you,
He alone raised a hand against them,
Saying the Chinese had taken him,
Again they arrayed themselves through the long day,
His neck rising above them,
In days when they could not be sated with booty,
The wretched one hung up the spoil,
Stained with dark blood,
Tearing up the earth in the middle,
His head seemed to touch the sky,
Making the whole world know,
A battered soul remained,
Raising a tomb as broad as an enclosure,
There they stood utterly bereft of counsel,
Standing and asking for counsel,
Ah, Jeljetpes, my khan and elder,
Speak, my living lion-hearted elder,
My true hero Jeljetpes, my elder,
Without sitting, they kindled a fire,
Without delay, they revived him like livestock,
He found a grave deep enough for us,
From the hands of the wrathful butcher,
He found no one who would be daunted.
Thinking wisely, he found many means,
He devised one stratagem and found a great one,
He found brushwood for the enclosures,
He found ground in which to dig a single grave,
Before three days had passed, ash rained down,
Across the Chinese host, ash rained down.
Into a mass of heavy hardship,
Being descendants of a khan,
Saying the enemy they sought would fall,
Like a station I had established,
Saying hero Tushkoz would arise,
It is a whirlwind in which his people vanished,
Now we understood it in our souls,
What remained of the booty,
What he took while begging for his head,
Valiant Kyrgyz, beloved people,
It became torment, elder brother,
Dear one, together with Chyn,
How few the Kyrgyz had become,
What remained of the booty,
How did the village settle?
What became of its stratagem?
So died my hundred heroes,
With his belt cast around his neck,
Pleading with Zhelzhetpes,
His soul exhausted as though by truth itself,
Roaring as he became resolute,
Falling into sorrow upon sorrow,
The enemy appeared before their eyes,
His means exhausted, he burned within,
O children, descending from life,
The musket fired its shot,
Blood and watery tears from both eyes,
Life burned like a fire,
He fashioned it from a thousand words,
Zhelzhetpes, who had seen it from childhood,
No soul could wrestle with Zhelzhetpes,
He stood asking for counsel,
He began firmly, speaking softly,
O, to the children of Chandayak,
He struck them with truthful words.
O, the two heroes of the pale one,
Those equal in their wish,
A bitter day met in humiliation,
The many Turkic oppressors,
No soul remains when showers of blows fall,
When battle begins again, no blood remains,
The Chinese host, while we stand alone,
What was done was broken before God,
The spreading circuit reached its limit,
Whirling around, it ravaged the land,
His head broken, God struck him,
Knowing the reason for the shot that was fired,
Take away the children's remaining lives,
The khan's horde began to move,
Hold your head, hero Korok,
Chyntemir entered the hero's work,
Your hope needs counsel,
Against the wrathful multitude,
Into hardship harder than stone,
From the venom of the true kinsmen,
From the wrath of true God,
If you touch us, children, we shall die,
A soul burdened with worldly sorrow,
The army suffered humiliation before the enemy,
We shall place it in a pouch and give it,
A wise man, a champion among men,
We shall die where death awaits,
Into what belonged to the elder brother,
Written in place of a remedy,
He began as an elder brother,
He guarded them as a forefather,
The sovereign Kyrgyz, beloved people,
Let us leave the hero upon the earth,
Let us set out before the soul departs,
Let us scatter the abundant wealth,
Come, children, let us remain,
You will know, Baisal, the host of my Manas.
He crossed three rivers,
He tethered his horse to a birch,
Traveling until he reached a comfortable place,
Ah, Jeljetpes was found,
Escaping from the wrathful enemy,
Thus enjoying days of ease,
In this way he settled himself.
A thousand Kazakhs stood on one side,
May Chyn Temir sink into the earth,
Only the fire between us has gone out,
Pursuing them as far as the pass,
To the farthest reaches of the land, to Jamysh,
Pursuing them across the land.
Beyond where the infidel’s eye could reach,
Pursuing them as far as the eye could see,
Would their waiting side begin the attack?
Their strength was worn away and gone,
Blood flowed through every valley,
Would he lead the people toward Tülkün?
There was no strength and none of that remained,
There was no soul left able to move,
Let us not act in ignorance,
Children, do not deliver the living to death,
Let us not hand them over from every side.
All sat down again,
Along the road that had been bound and given,
The noble one toward death,
They ended by driving him onward,
Now he has gone to that place,
A khan who could strike many went there,
Enough—defeated by the enemy,
Having come to such a pass,
Heed my words, children; let us go.
We shall move onward from the open country,
Let us go to the place he went,
Taking what is needed for the horde,
Let us reach the place where he lies.
Three sharp trials, this hard world,
Let us swing and strike with full reach.
That soul endured seven circuits.
Let us summon the obedient boys.
So saying, seven rose in defiance.
Poor wanderer, beyond the wind’s reach,
The orphaned man sharpened his resolve.
They made his daughters reveal the secret.
Speaking truth as in the old age,
They spoke of that hardship as a trial.
In the place where two stood upright,
Brave Kuman stood his equal.
Thus Kenen set forth his terror.
When the people heard it, all gathered.
The noble head was torn to pieces.
The lion was beyond the wind’s reach.
We were the elder brothers who kept watch.
We were the angry heroes who arrived.
Our elder brother held it in his hand.
You were life itself.
At last we shall take the outside road.
We had not yet looked to the heroic man.
What land was free from trouble?
Our mother spoke and reached us.
He had not yet left this plank.
He had not fallen while walking in prayer.
The child had not yet known hardship.
Rib and body had not yet hardened.
The great village knew the truth.
He had not yet lain down in this wrath.
No other village had yet been struck.
The sheath of childhood had not remained.
Alas, to be overtaken by grief.
The light of hero Kenen,
His daughter endured it and gave her life.
Longing flowed, and she gave a child.
You opened his eyes.
The dark center of the true eye,
The son of true Kenen,
Lying there only in contentment,
The God of this possession of mine,
O elder Zhelzhetpes,
You saw him fall in joy,
The sword flashed as it was drawn,
From firing straight toward advantage,
If you die, my thought will be empty,
You saw his eyes fall,
Where did you fall upon the earth?
I asked you, great young champion,
If there is wisdom, dear champion,
Friend of your youth, dear champion,
If Kenen comes and takes him,
Warrior people inherited from the forefather,
The white-capped Kyrgyz people,
What shall we do now?
O God, when the people gathered as one,
Deeds performed by a hero, O child,
Alas, the enemy disappeared,
Ala-Too, which became our father,
By the wish of Zhelzhetpes,
Elder, what shall we do without the hero?
Bringing the warrior's head low,
Turning every foremost man into a champion,
Turning one land into humiliation,
His descent after fleeing,
See Kenen's blood,
